西北太平洋是全球热带气旋活动最活跃的海域之一，台风的生成数量、移动路径与强度变化，直接影响航运航线规划、航行安全及企业经济效益。云遥宇航气导团队依托 2000-2025 年西北太平洋热带气旋历史统计数据，结合 ENSO（厄尔尼诺-南方涛动）、PDO（太平洋年代际涛动）等关键气候模态的最新预测结果，以及欧洲中期天气预报中心（ECMWF）数值模拟数据，对 2026 年该海域热带气旋活动趋势展开综合研判分析，为航运企业的经营决策、风险防控提供专业参考依据。

根据2000年至2025年命名台风数量的统计，每年西北太平洋台风数量在25个左右，其中最多35个（2013年），最少17个（2023年）。统计台风路径经过各海区的次数，其中南海、东海出现频率最大，南海每年约12次左右，东海每年约8次左右。黄海和渤海出现次数一般小于2次。
![](/media/news/gzhImg4_260701103147A198.webp)
![](/media/news/newsImg15_260701103206A199.webp)

### 一、关键气候模态对热带气旋的影响及 2026年预测

西北太平洋热带气旋的频率、强度及生成位置，与 ENSO、PDO等大尺度气候模态存在显著的直接或间接关联，二者的相位变化共同主导着热带气旋的活动规律。

#### （一）ENSO 模态：2026 年夏季起厄尔尼诺将成主导状态
ENSO 是热带太平洋海域典型的海气耦合振荡现象，具有 2-7 年的周期变化，分为厄尔尼诺（赤道中东太平洋海温异常偏暖）和拉尼娜（赤道中东太平洋海温异常偏冷）两个相位，其通过改变热带太平洋海温、对流活动及沃克环流，对全球天气气候及热带气旋活动产生深远影响。

结合 Nino 3.4 海表温度的动力模型与统计模型预测结果，2026 年 ENSO 相位将呈现明显的阶段性变化：2026 年 2-4 月 ENSO 中性状态的发生概率高达 96%，且该中性状态将持续至 3-5 月、4-6 月；此期间厄尔尼诺发生概率逐步提升，从 3-5 月的 9% 增至 4-6 月的 35%，并在 5-7 月成为主导状态；2026 年北半球夏季至秋季（6-12 月），厄尔尼诺将持续占据主导，发生概率稳定在 58%-61%。

厄尔尼诺相位对西北太平洋热带气旋的影响主要体现在生成位置和强度时长两方面：一是生成数量与气候平均值基本持平，但生成位置整体偏东、偏南，西太平洋东南海域热带气旋生成频率显著增加，而日本南部与台湾东部海域生成频率则明显降低；二是热带气旋强度偏强、持续时间更长，强台风出现的概率显著高于气候平均水平。

![](/media/news/gzhImg5_260701103345A200.webp)
（由哥伦比亚大学气候学院国际气候与社会研究所提供）

#### （二）PDO 模态：2026 全年维持冷相位，延续 2025 年影响模式

PDO 是太平洋海表温度与气压异常的长期波动模式，时间尺度可达 10-20 年甚至数十年，分为暖相位（PDO 指数为正）和冷相位（PDO 指数为负）：暖相位时北太平洋中部海温偏低、太平洋东部及北美西海岸海温偏暖；冷相位时北太平洋中部海温偏暖、东太平洋海温偏冷。

根据美国国家海洋和大气管理局（NOAA）气候预测中心 CFS 模型预估结果，2026 年全年 PDO 指数将维持负值，即 PDO 模态持续处于冷相位，且与 2025 年的相位状态基本一致，对台风活动的总体影响将延续去年模式。

PDO 冷相位为西北太平洋热带气旋生成提供了有利的气候背景：一方面，西太平洋海表温度偏暖、对流活动增强，有利于台风扰动的发展和热带气旋的生成，推动西北太平洋热带气旋全年生成数量或活动指数偏高，且该关联在年代际尺度上表现尤为显著；另一方面，冷相位下西太平洋副热带高压较常年偏弱，南海及菲律宾以东地区 500hPa 位势高度偏低，利于季风槽形成，同时南海至菲律宾一带高空西风、低空西南风异常偏强，低层正涡度、低海平面气压、强对流等特征显著，这些条件不仅利于热带气旋生成，还会增强影响华南地区的台风强度，使得达到台风及以上强度的热带气旋在影响华南的总数中占比偏大。

### 二、2026 年西北太平洋热带气旋整体活动趋势

结合 ENSO、PDO 两大气候模态的预测结果及二者的相互作用，再叠加欧洲中期天气预报中心（ECMWF）2026 年 2 月发布的热带气旋密度指数预测数据，2026 年西北太平洋热带气旋活动将呈现以下核心特征：

**强度偏强、持续时间较长**：2026 年夏季起 ENSO 将由中性状态转为厄尔尼诺主导，叠加 PDO 全年冷相位的协同作用，二者形成的非线性效应将推动北太平洋热带气旋平均强度偏强，且单个热带气旋的持续时间整体长于气候平均值，强台风出现的概率提升。

**生成位置偏东偏南**：受厄尔尼诺相位的主导影响，2026 年西北太平洋热带气旋的生成位置将整体偏东、偏南，西太平洋东南海域生成频率增加，而日本南部、台湾东部海域生成频率有所降低，热带气旋的源地分布发生明显偏移。

**部分海域影响频率偏高**：根据 ECMWF 热带气旋密度指数预测（表征经过目标位置 300 公里范围内的热带气旋数量异常），2026 年未来 6 个月内，中国东部海域、菲律宾东部海域的热带气旋路径密度高于气候平均值，受热带气旋影响的频率较常年偏高，相关海域需重点关注台风活动。

![](/media/news/gzhImg6_260701103603A201.webp)

**华南地区面临强台风威胁**：PDO 冷相位延续使得影响华南地区的台风强度偏强，达到台风及以上等级的占比偏大，华南沿海成为 2026 年台风防灾减灾的重点区域。

综合目前可得到数据资料分析，云遥宇航气导得出以下预测结果，2026年西北太平洋热带气旋活动整体偏活跃，呈现强度较往年偏强、生成位置偏东南，且中国东部、菲律宾东部海域受影响频次偏高，华南沿海面临强台风威胁的特征。航运企业可结合这一趋势，提前做好经营规划、完善预案。云遥宇航气导团队依托自有卫星数据和多源权威数据，持续关注并动态更新台风发展预测、精准研判海域气象风险。若您有航线气象保障等相关需求，欢迎与我们联系，云遥专业气导服务为您保驾护航！
Analysis of Tropical Cyclone Activity Trends in the Northwest Pacific in 2026

The Northwest Pacific Ocean is one of the most active sea areas for tropical cyclone activities worldwide. The number of typhoons generated, their movement paths, and changes in intensity directly affect shipping route planning, navigation safety, and the economic benefits of enterprises. The Cloud Remote Sensing Aerospace Guidance team, based on the historical data of tropical cyclones in the Northwest Pacific Ocean from 2000 to 2025, combined with the latest prediction results of key climate modes such as ENSO (El Niño-Southern Oscillation) and PDO (Pacific Decadal Oscillation), as well as the numerical simulation data from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), conducted a comprehensive analysis and assessment of the trend of tropical cyclone activities in this area in 2026, providing professional reference basis for the business decisions and risk prevention of shipping enterprises. 

Based on the statistics of the number of named typhoons from 2000 to 2025, the number of typhoons in the Northwest Pacific Ocean is approximately 25 each year, with the maximum being 35 (in 2013) and the minimum being 17 (in 2023). The statistics also show the frequency of typhoons passing through each sea area. Among them, the South China Sea and the East China Sea have the highest occurrence rates. The South China Sea has about 12 occurrences per year, and the East China Sea has about 8 occurrences per year. The occurrences in the Yellow Sea and the Bohai Sea are generally less than 2 times.

![](/media/news/gzhImg4_260701103755A202.webp)
![](/media/news/newsImg15_260701103811A203.webp)

### I. The Impact of Key Climate Modes on Tropical Cyclones and Forecast for 2026

The frequency, intensity and generation location of tropical cyclones in the Northwest Pacific are significantly and directly or indirectly correlated with large-scale climate modes such as ENSO and PDO. The phase changes of these two factors jointly dominate the activity patterns of tropical cyclones.

#### (1) ENSO Mode: From the summer of 2026, El Niño will become the dominant state.

ENSO is a typical sea-air coupled oscillation phenomenon in the tropical Pacific Ocean, with a period variation of 2 to 7 years. It is divided into two phases: El Niño (where the sea temperature in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean is abnormally warm) and La Niña (where the sea temperature in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean is abnormally cold). Through changes in the sea temperature of the tropical Pacific, convective activities, and the Walker circulation, it has a profound impact on global weather and climate as well as tropical cyclone activities. 

Combining the results of the dynamical model and the statistical model of the Nino 3.4 sea surface temperature, the ENSO phase in 2026 will show a significant phased change: The probability of the ENSO neutral state occurring in February to April of 2026 is as high as 96%, and this neutral state will last until March to May and April to June; during this period, the probability of El Niño gradually increases, from 9% in March to May to 35% in April to June, and it becomes the dominant state in May to July; from the summer to autumn (June to December) of the Northern Hemisphere in 2026, El Niño will continue to dominate, with a stable occurrence probability of 58% to 61%. 

The influence of the El Niño phase on tropical cyclones in the Northwest Pacific Ocean is mainly reflected in two aspects: Firstly, the number of tropical cyclones generated is basically the same as the climatic average, but the generation locations are generally shifted to the east and south. The frequency of tropical cyclone generation in the eastern and southern waters of the Western Pacific has significantly increased, while the generation frequency in the waters off southern Japan and eastern Taiwan has decreased significantly. Secondly, the intensity of tropical cyclones is stronger and their duration is longer. The probability of strong typhoons occurring is significantly higher than the climatic average.

![](/media/news/gzhImg5_260701104022A204.webp)
(Provided by the International Climate and Society Institute of the Columbia University Climate School)

#### (2) PDO Mode: The cold phase will persist throughout 2026, continuing the influence pattern observed in 2025.

PDO refers to the long-term fluctuation pattern of sea surface temperature and air pressure anomalies in the Pacific Ocean, with a time scale ranging from 10 to 20 years or even several decades. It is divided into the warm phase (where the PDO index is positive) and the cold phase (where the PDO index is negative): during the warm phase, the sea temperature in the central part of the North Pacific is lower, while the sea temperature in the eastern Pacific and the west coast of North America is higher; during the cold phase, the sea temperature in the central part of the North Pacific is higher, and the sea temperature in the eastern Pacific is lower. 

According to the forecast results of the CFS model of the Climate Prediction Center of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), the PDO index for the entire year of 2026 will remain negative, meaning the PDO mode will continue to be in a cold phase, and it will be basically the same as the phase state in 2025. The overall impact on typhoon activities will continue the pattern of last year. 

The cold phase of PDO provides a favorable climatic background for the formation of tropical cyclones in the Northwest Pacific: On the one hand, the sea surface temperature in the Western Pacific is warmer and the convective activity is enhanced, which is conducive to the development of typhoon disturbances and the formation of tropical cyclones, promoting a higher number of tropical cyclones or activity index throughout the year in the Northwest Pacific, and this correlation is particularly significant on an interdecadal scale; on the other hand, in the cold phase, the subtropical high in the Western Pacific is weaker than normal, and the 500 hPa geopotential height in the South China Sea and east of the Philippines is lower, which is conducive to the formation of the monsoon trough. At the same time, the upper-level westerly wind and lower-level southwesterly wind in the South China Sea to the east of the Philippines are abnormally strong, and the low-level positive vorticity, low sea level pressure, and strong convective activities are significant. These conditions not only facilitate the formation of tropical cyclones, but also enhance the intensity of typhoons affecting South China, resulting in a larger proportion of tropical cyclones reaching typhoon or above intensity among those affecting South China.

### II. Overall Activity Trend of Tropical Cyclones in the Northwest Pacific in 2026

Based on the prediction results of the two major climate modes (ENSO and PDO) and their interactions, and by adding the tropical cyclone density index prediction data released by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) in February 2026, the tropical cyclone activities in the Northwest Pacific in 2026 will exhibit the following core characteristics:

**Strong intensity and long duration:** Starting from the summer of 2026, ENSO will shift from a neutral state to being dominated by El Niño. Coupled with the consistent cold phase of PDO throughout the year, the nonlinear effect formed by the two will drive the average intensity of tropical cyclones in the North Pacific to be stronger than normal, and the duration of individual tropical cyclones will be overall longer than the climatic average. The probability of strong typhoons will increase. 

**Generation location is more to the east and south:** Dominated by the El Niño phase, the generation location of tropical cyclones in the Northwest Pacific in 2026 will be generally shifted to the east and south. The generation frequency in the eastern waters of the Western Pacific will increase, while the generation frequency in the waters off southern Japan and eastern Taiwan will decrease. The distribution of the source areas of tropical cyclones has significantly shifted. 

**The frequency of impact in some sea areas is relatively high:** According to the ECMWF tropical cyclone density index prediction (indicating the abnormal number of tropical cyclones within a 300-kilometer radius passing through the target location), in the next 6 months of 2026, the density of tropical cyclone paths in the eastern sea areas of China and the eastern sea areas of the Philippines is higher than the climatic average. The frequency of being affected by tropical cyclones is higher than usual, and the relevant sea areas need to pay close attention to the activities of typhoons.

![](/media/news/gzhImg6_260701104311A205.webp)

**The South China region is under threat from strong typhoons:** The continuation of the cold phase of the PDO has led to stronger typhoons affecting the South China region, with a higher proportion reaching typhoon or above levels. The coastal areas of South China have become the key areas for typhoon disaster prevention and mitigation in 2026.

Based on the analysis of the available data, the Cloud-Rover Aerospace Inertial Guidance System has made the following predictions: In 2026, the overall activity of tropical cyclones in the Northwest Pacific will be more active. The intensity will be stronger than in previous years, and the generation locations will be more to the southeast. Moreover, the eastern part of China and the eastern waters of the Philippines will experience higher frequencies of being affected, and the coastal areas of South China will face the threat of strong typhoons. Shipping companies can combine this trend and make advance business planning and improve contingency plans.
